first.rationale: The competitor’s entry pricing directly threatens the price-sensitive SMB segment where targeted promotional pricing previously showed acquisition and revenue lift. I will verify the pricing result and the onboarding result before committing, since declining onboarding completion may affect whether pricing-led acquisition converts into durable qualified revenue.

mid.rationale: Run a shortened/simplified onboarding experiment. The verified source record showed completion up 13%, time-to-value down 2.1 days, and 30-day retention up 3%, directly addressing the current 4% completion decline while supporting sustainable downstream value. Promotional pricing is excluded because its verified short-term revenue lift came with 30-day retention down 12%. Monitor qualified-revenue conversion and retention by acquired cohort, since the prior onboarding result did not directly report qualified revenue.

final2.rationale: Keep the onboarding simplification experiment. It is the only directly supported option that improves completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, while signup simplification also durably improved SMB activation. The deeper competitor cut raises urgency, but the available pricing evidence shows a 40% targeted discount increased qualified revenue while reducing 30-day retention by 12%; it does not establish that discounting prevents churn among existing SMB accounts. Monitor price-sensitive SMB churn and qualified-revenue conversion closely; a retention-specific pricing response remains uncertain and should not displace the proven sustainable-value intervention this cycle.
